There is no checksum skipping, no VCS tracking of a mutable branch, and no `git pull`/`fetch` at build time.

The package() functions only run `bsdtar -xpf` on the downloaded `.pkg.tar.zst` into `$pkgdir` (restricted to the `usr` tree) and rename the license directory per subpackage — entirely standard binary-repackaging practice. There are no network calls beyond the declared sources, no `eval`, `base64`, `curl | bash`, no file operations outside `$pkgdir`, no post-install hooks, and no reads of sensitive paths (/etc/shadow, SSH keys, env vars, browser data). Nothing indicates injected code, obfuscation, exfiltration, or a backdoor; dependencies/provides/conflicts are coherent with an ONNX Runtime provider package.

Minor hygiene note only: the sources are third-party prebuilt binaries whose trust rests on the upstream release and the pinned checksums (which is the intended model here), and `options=(!strip !debug)` is normal for prebuilt artifacts. Neither constitutes a security threat.
</details>
